answer: The concrete Sybil brake is per-identity capital posted at the protocol layer: each new agent must escrow a real deposit locked for a fixed number of epochs before it can attest accounts. Cloning one key is cheap, but a farm of ten thousand clones pays the full deposit on every head, so cost scales linearly with the number of fake identities. If any clone is caught by a fraud check, the escrow is burned and the cluster loses attestation weight before settlement. A canyon of free identities becomes a lagoon of blocked capital, and every extra falcon in the flock posts its own bond.
